title: 80 Acres Farms shutting down San Antonio site, lay off 166
content:
A failed business acquisition led 80 Acres Farms to shutter its operations at the Brooks facility, resulting in 166 employees being laid off. 

A failed business acquisition led 80 Acres Farms to shutter its operations at the Brooks facility, resulting in 166 employees being laid off.

Ohio-based 80 Acres Farms is shutting down its operations, including a vertical grow operation on the South Side, after a deal to sell the company fell through. [...] Mike Zelkind, the CEO and co-founder of Hamilton, Ohio-based company, said in a Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification letter that the business was permanently shutting down all of its operations across the nation after a prospective buyer “unexpectedly withdrew from the transaction” on Aug. 2.

READ MORE:At an indoor vertical farm on San Antonio’s South Side, robots and humans grow herbs and greens [...] The vertical farming business notified the Texas Workforce Commission that it will lay off 166 workers at its San Antonio operations at Brooks. The layoffs, which started Monday, are expected to be complete by Aug. 17.

title: 80 Acres Farms shutdown triggers wave of lawsuits
content:
In the federal lawsuit filed Aug. 6 in Delaware, four former employees, one from the Hamilton location, one from its Aurora, Colo. facility and one from its San Antonio, Texas facility, claim 80 Acres Farms illegally terminated hundreds of workers across multiple states without providing the required 60‑day notice as the indoor‑agriculture company abruptly ceased operations last month. [...] The lawsuit outlines shutdowns at facilities in Colorado, Georgia, Indiana, Kentucky, Ohio South Carolina, Texas and Washington.

The suit seeks class‑action status and says roughly 500 employees let go "as part of, or as the foreseeable result of" the ordered mass layoffs or plant closures. None received the 60‑day written notice required under the federal Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act, according to the filing. [...] According to the complaint, the four employees learned of their terminations between July 30 and Aug. 4.

The suit also claims 80 Acres offered some workers three weeks of severance pay but never provided it. The lawsuit seeks 60 days of back pay and benefits for all affected workers, along with attorneys' fees and interest.

Earlier this month, the plaintiffs filed a notice of bankruptcy suggestion, signaling that 80 Acres' financial collapse could affect the lawsuit.

title: Elon Musk's Brother's 'Smart Farm' Startup Lays Off Most Staff - Business Insider
content: Square Roots CEO Tobias Peggs, who cofounded the company alongside Kimbal Musk, notified employees on a Zoom call on Tuesday that the startup would halt production at its locations in Springfield, Ohio, Shepherdsville, Kentucky, and Kenosha, Wisconsin, the two sources said. Kenosha News was the first to report that the Wisconsin location was facing a shutdown and WDRB later confirmed the company planned to shut down four of its farms. [...] The company shut down its original farm in Brooklyn earlier this year, laying off about 50 people at the time, according to a January press release.The recent layoffs came across as a surprise to staff, the ex-employees said. Square Roots had only just opened the Kenosha facility — its largest yet— in August and its Shepherdsville location had been operational for less than three months, they told Insider. [...] Square Roots, a tech farming startup that was cofounded by Elon Musk's brother, Kimbal, shut down the majority of its remaining locations on Tuesday and laid off most of its staff, two employees who were laid off as a result of the closures told Insider.

title: Revol Greens may close Owatonna greenhouse and lay off 89 workers | MPR News
content:
The lettuce grower told state regulators Wednesday that it would be forced to close its Medford facility about an hour south of the Twin Cites and layoff approximately 89 employees if the site or company does not secure financing or get bought out before Oct. 4.

John Carkoski, Revol Greens Vice President of Operations, emphasized in a press release Friday that Revol Greens is still committed to finding a path forward. [...] “Our leafy greens are grown year-round in our controlled-environment greenhouses in Minnesota and Texas, where every step of the growing process is designed with food safety in mind,” the company wrote on its Facebook page in mid July. “From treated water and plant and mineral based fertilizers, to automated harvesting that minimizes human handling, our growing practices help us maintain a highly controlled environment from seed to harvest.” [...] Skip to Main Content
